articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor left AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like breadcrumbs for nation-state actors. The agency that's supposed to protect infrastructure just handed out the keys to the kingdom—again.

articles.title: Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor
articles.summary: Cisco patches a perfect 10.0 CVSS flaw in Secure Workload that lets unauthenticated attackers waltz right into sensitive data. When your 'secure' workload isn't.

articles.title: Microsoft warns of new Defender zero-days exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft's Defender actively exploited in the wild for privilege escalation and DoS. The irony of security software being weaponized against itself never gets old.

articles.title: Attackers spill plaintext passwords of 46k Myspace93 users after 2021 breach
articles.summary: HackerOne slashes bug bounty payouts by 75% for critical flaws. Nothing says 'we value security researchers' like paying them in exposure and disappointment.

articles.title: Trump Mobile Hit With Fresh Humiliation
articles.summary: GitHub confirms 3,800 internal repos stolen via poisoned VS Code extension. TeamPCP pwned the platform where everyone stores their code—meta irony at its finest.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google API keys remain exploitable for 23 minutes after 'deletion' despite claims of immediate revocation. Because apparently 'immediate' means something different in Mountain View.

articles.title: Microsoft issues YellowKey mitigation, no patch yet
articles.summary: Nine-year-old Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw finally discovered. Sometimes the best hiding spot is right under everyone's nose for nearly a decade.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a win for end-to-end encryption against the eternal crusade of governments wanting to read everyone's love letters. Privacy advocates: 1, Surveillance state: Still trying.

articles.title: China's Webworm Uses Discord, Microsoft Graphs to Hack EU Govts.
articles.summary: EFF's new guide fights back against normalized digital surveillance abuses in the Americas. Because someone has to remind people that mass surveillance isn't supposed to be normal.

articles.title: Cisco Patches CVSS 10.0 Secure Workload REST API Flaw Enabling Data Access
articles.summary: CISA adds exploited Langflow and Trend Micro flaws to KEV catalog. Another day, another batch of vulnerabilities being actively weaponized in the wild.
